noches-de-velaluz.pitch: Friday concert nights on the Paseo, eight weeks each spring and fall.
description: Noches de Velaluz is the island's concert series. For eight Fridays in the spring and eight in the fall, a stage goes up at the waterfront end of Paseo Velaluz and the promenade stays open late.
The concerts are free, but you need to register in advance because the waterfront has a capacity. Register one household at a time, for as many nights as you like.

festival-de-las-linternas.pitch: Six weeks of lanterns at Costa Encandela, from mid November to the end of the year.
description: Festival de las Linternas is the island's holiday season. From November 15 to December 29 the park is hung with thousands of extra lanterns, and the evening ends with a lantern procession from the lighthouse to the front gate.
The festival is included with park admission and needs no registration. These are some of the busiest weeks of the year, so expect peak-date ticket prices.

tormenta-nights.pitch: October after dark at Punta Tormenta, when the storm theme gets turned all the way up.
description: Tormenta Nights runs through October. The park stays open into the evening with fog, lightning effects and street performers on every walkway, and the coasters run in the dark.
It is included with park admission. It is louder and darker than a normal evening, and most families with small children find Costa Encandela a better choice on these nights.

paseo-food-and-rhythm-festival.pitch: Two weeks of food stalls and live music on the Paseo each May.
description: The Paseo Food and Rhythm Festival fills the promenade from May 3 to May 18. Restaurants set up tasting stalls outside their doors, and bands play at both ends of the Paseo through the evening.
There is no gate and no ticket. Paseo Velaluz is open to everyone, whether or not you are visiting a park that day.
